200.description: Bootstrap config; update.decision is none|recommended|required, where required comes from updatePolicy.minSupportedVersion or from a mandatory active release. wallet.tokens lists the token catalogue for the app (BootstrapWalletToken[]): only enabled tokens on the tenant's enabled chains, tenant rows override global rows with the same (chain, address), sorted by sortWeight DESC then symbol ASC; it never carries verified/id/scope (the app grants verified from its own allowlist). wallet.tokens is required by the app schema; every enabled chain carries an enabled native entry, and every delivered row is validated before delivery (a corrupt row makes the whole bootstrap fail with 503 rather than being repaired on the read path); services.predict (domain, scopeId, chain) is present only while modules.predict is enabled and is 503 when enabled but not configured. Optional installation authentication: a request carrying X-Installation-ID plus Authorization: Installation <credential> is matched against canary releases, so the device may receive update.full/update.ota for a canary build instead of the active one; an absent, expired or revoked credential is treated as anonymous and only ever sees active (bootstrap itself never fails on a credential problem). update.canary.enrolled says whether the offered full release is a canary build; update.canary.otaToken is a 24h opaque token that the app must store with Updates.setExtraParamAsync("canary-token", token) so the native manifest request can be matched to a canary OTA revision (the key must stay lowercase: expo-structured-headers rejects uppercase dictionary keys). otaToken is null when the installation could not be authenticated, and the app then clears the stored param. update.minSupportedVersion and the mandatory flag always come from the active release, never from a canary one features.directUpdateEnabled is additionally false when the requesting build and the release it would install were signed with different certificates (the platform installer would reject the in-app install after the download), so the client falls back to opening the download URL instead of looping a failing install.

get.summary: Tenant OTA code signing key (public facts only)
get.description: Returns {configured, keyId, certificatePem, certificateSha256, certificateSubject, certificateNotBefore, certificateNotAfter, version, updatedBy, updatedAt}. The private key is never returned by any endpoint: it is stored encrypted with the storage master key and can only be replaced, not read back. The validity window is exposed because an expired certificate cannot be replaced over the air; only a native release can.

put.summary: Install or rotate the tenant OTA code signing key
put.description: Stores an RSA private key (PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 PEM, >= 2048 bits) encrypted at rest, together with the certificate the app compiles in. The certificate must match the private key: a mismatch would make every device silently reject updates and stay on the embedded bundle, so it is refused at write time. Signatures are emitted as the RFC 8941 `expo-signature` dictionary (sig/keyid/alg=rsa-v1_5-sha256) over the final response bytes.

200.description: Saved signing key status (same shape as GET)

400.description: INVALID_OTA_SIGNING_KEY: key is not RSA/too small/malformed, certificate does not match the key, missing reason or confirm

409.description: STALE_OTA_SIGNING_KEY: expectedVersion does not match the stored version

post.summary: Generate the tenant OTA code signing key on the server
post.description: Generates an RSA key pair and a self-signed code signing certificate, then stores them like PUT does. The private key is never returned: the server must already hold it in the clear to sign every manifest, so generating it here adds no exposure, but it removes the plaintext file, the cross-machine transfer and the shred discipline that the manual ceremony depends on. The certificate carries X509v3 Key Usage: Digital Signature and Extended Key Usage: Code Signing, which is exactly what expo-updates' CertificateChain checks; NotBefore is backdated five minutes because the client validates against the device clock. There is no offline backup: losing this key costs a native release, which is also what rotating it costs.

200.description: Saved signing key status (same shape as GET); the private key is not included

400.description: INVALID_OTA_SIGNING_KEY: keySize out of range, years out of range, missing reason or confirm

409.description: STALE_OTA_SIGNING_KEY: expectedVersion does not match the stored version

get.description: Returns {configured, keyAlias, keystoreSha256, version, updatedBy, updatedAt}. The sealed bundle itself is never returned to admin readers; only the build-agent channel receives it. The server cannot open the bundle in any case: it is sealed with an operator passphrase the server does not have, and the server only wraps it with the storage master key on top.

put.summary: Upload the sealed Android signing keystore
put.description: Accepts a bundle produced by `build-keystore seal` on the operator's machine. The server validates the envelope shape and the KDF parameters, wraps it with the storage master key and stores it per tenant. It deliberately cannot decrypt the inner bundle: the Android signing key is never used by the server at runtime, and a leak of it cannot be remediated for direct distribution, so the server must not hold the ability to read it.

post.description: Atomically claims the oldest queued job for the requested platforms (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two agents never get the same job) and returns its parameters together with the tenant slug and the tenant OTA code signing certificate. The private key is never returned. Shipping the certificate with the job is what keeps the certificate compiled into the app in sync with the key the server signs with. Returns 204 when the queue is empty. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token, a credential kept separate from the admin key: a compromised build machine should yield the build queue, not the whole admin surface.

200.description: Claimed build job with tenantSlug and otaCertificatePem

post.description: Moves the job to running and stores a bounded log tail (at most 200 lines, 2000 bytes each). Authenticated with x-build-agent-token, a credential kept separate from the admin key: a compromised build machine should yield the build queue, not the whole admin surface.

commitSha and artifactSha256 must be lowercase hex digests; the server records what was built, not how. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token, a credential kept separate from the admin key: a compromised build machine should yield the build queue, not the whole admin surface.

failureReason is required: a failure with no reason shows up in the admin UI as failed with nothing to act on. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token, a credential kept separate from the admin key: a compromised build machine should yield the build queue, not the whole admin surface.

post.summary: Create an artifact upload ticket for a running build
post.description: Same ticket the admin upload flow issues, scoped to the job's tenant. The upload URL points at the build-agent channel because the agent holds no admin credential. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token; the job id scopes the request to that job's tenant.

put.description: Proxy-mode upload of the APK; direct mode uploads straight to object storage with the presigned URL from the ticket. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token; the job id scopes the request to that job's tenant.

post.summary: Turn the uploaded artifact into a release record
post.description: Platform, version, build number and release notes are all taken from the build job row, never from the request body: those define the artifact's identity and what users will read, and the job row already passed validation. Runs the same APK identity inspection, ETag pinning and signer fingerprint gate as a manual upload. Authenticated with x-build-agent-token; the job id scopes the request to that job's tenant.

signerSha256.description: SHA-256 of the production signing certificate, 64 hex chars (colons and upper case accepted, normalised)

expectedVersion.description: Optimistic lock: current stored version, 0 when unset

appleTeamId.description: Apple Developer Team ID, 10 alphanumeric characters (lower case accepted, normalised to upper case)

bundleId.description: iOS bundle identifier of the tenant production build

expectedVersion.description: Optimistic lock: current stored version, 0 when unset

privateKeyPem.description: RSA private key, PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 PEM, at least 2048 bits. Stored encrypted; never returned.

certificatePem.description: The code signing certificate the app compiles in. Must match privateKeyPem.

expectedVersion.description: Optimistic lock: current stored version, 0 when unset

years.description: Certificate lifetime. An expired certificate cannot be replaced over the air; only a native release can.

expectedVersion.description: Optimistic lock: current stored version, 0 when unset

gitRef.description: Branch name or commit sha to build

buildNumber.description: Android versionCode / iOS build; must strictly increase

releaseNotes.description: Release notes by language code, one array entry per line. Carried on the job because the release record is created by the build agent and there is no endpoint to edit notes afterwards.

agent.description: Self-reported build machine identity; recorded for triage only, never used for authorization

platforms.description: Platforms this agent can build; empty means both

commitSha.description: The commit actually checked out, lowercase hex

releaseId.description: app_releases row the artifact landed in, when the agent uploaded it

commitSha.description: The commit the agent had checked out, when it got that far; a failed build still needs to say which revision it tried

SealedKeystore.description: scrypt + AES-256-GCM envelope produced on the operator's machine. The server checks the shape and refuses weakened KDF parameters, but never holds the passphrase.

keystoreSha256.description: sha256 of the keystore file, so operators can tell which key a tenant is set to sign with
